content.title: About
content.content: Barbecue-flavored potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes fried to a crisp and coated with a smoky, sweet‑savory spice blend that mimics the taste of barbecue. They are a popular snack often enjoyed at movies, picnics, and as a quick bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial potato chip brand appeared in the early 1920s in the United States.
Barbecue flavor is achieved with smoked paprika, sugar, onion, garlic, and a mix of spices.
Depending on the cooking method, chips can contain up to 30% fat.
In Russia, barbecue chips are often confused with “smoked bacon” flavored chips.
There are low‑calorie baked versions where the potatoes are oven‑cooked instead of fried.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Chips provide carbohydrates that deliver quick energy, useful during travel or active events.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C remains in potatoes, especially when chips are cooked at lower temperatures.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Excess salt can raise blood pressure, so moderation is recommended.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of fat and carbs, frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes include dairy or soy additives that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy chips straight from the bag, use them as a crunchy topping for sandwiches, salads, or incorporate them into dishes like baked vegetables for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed bag or airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to retain crispness and flavor.
